blocks.text: The state asks for all continuations from i. Every continuation begins with either a one-step or a two-step move, after which the remaining count is dp(i + 1) or dp(i + 2). Because those groups are disjoint and exhaustive, their counts add. Overlap may make this recurrence worth memoizing, but overlap alone does not supply the recurrence or its aggregation operator.

blocks.text: The skip branch leaves capacity unchanged and moves to i + 1. The take branch is available only when the item fits; it adds v[i], subtracts its weight, and also moves to i + 1 to enforce single use. Every part follows from the state and problem contract. An incomplete index-only state could not express the capacity guard, while a transition that keeps i silently changes the archetype.

messages.text: The take branch neither consumes capacity nor checks feasibility, so it can select overweight items and overstate the optimum.
Keeping i after taking allows the same item to be selected repeatedly; that is an unbounded-choice transition, not 0/1 selection.

Those trade-offs come after the transition is fixed.

blocks.text: The uncompressed take branch reads dp from the previous item layer. In one array, that value is preserved only if capacities are processed descending; then c - w has not yet been updated for the current item. Ascending order lets the current item contribute repeatedly within one layer. Compression therefore requires a revised operational transition whose reads still represent the intended logical states.

blocks.text: Sentinel choice is part of the transition contract. In a maximization where legitimate values may be negative, zero is not harmless: it can appear better than every feasible branch. Negative infinity ensures the branch cannot win, while explicit guards avoid creating it at all. For minimization the polarity reverses, and counting usually excludes impossible branches or assigns them zero ways.

messages.text: Positive infinity would always win a maximization and make the result invalid.
Zero can beat valid negative solutions and fabricate a feasible outcome that the transition never earned.

feedback.reason: An impossible branch must be dominated by every valid maximization result, so -infinity or explicit exclusion preserves semantics.

options.text: Use -infinity or exclude the branch so it cannot win the maximum.

blocks.text: Legal moves determine that right and down are the dependencies in both problems. The output contract then supplies the algebra: sum for the cardinality of disjoint path sets, and minimum for choosing one cheapest continuation, with current cost added. Reusing a graph shape does not mean reusing its aggregation operator. This distinction transfers to boolean feasibility using OR and maximum reward using max.
